newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may launch 10 pct fixed rate bonds in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia may launch 10 pct fixed rate bonds in 1997.

text.p: The Russian Central Bank may start issuing 80 trillion roubles of 10 percent fixed-rate bonds with maturities up to 15 years later this year, a senior bank official said on Thursday.

"It seems that some time in the future this year, or maybe the beginning of next year, we will quote this paper on the securities market," Konstantin Korishchenko, director of the bank's open-market operations department, told a CS First Boston investors conference.
Korishchenko noted the rate on the paper, securitised from central bank loans to the Finance Ministry over 1992 to 1994, was far below current yields of 30-32 percent on GKO discount Treasury bills.
"We have not yet begun to sell this paper because we would take a big discount," he said.
The central bank has already started to issue 20 percent fixed-rate three-year bonds, also securitised from central bank loans to the government, which have gone down well.
Foreign investors have proved willing to buy long-dated Russian paper but are also keen to buy fixed-rate securities, Russian dealers and salesmen said.

Except for the recent small issue of three-year fixed rate bonds, anything with a maturity of more than one year pays a floating-rate coupon, subject to sharp changes, deterring some potential investors.
